Compact Bias-Variance Lab Script
nodes.rationale: A compact executable implementation that simulates average fits and learning curves for two targets and three models.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance and Learning-Curve Results JSON
nodes.rationale: Stores analytical/simulation bias-variance results and learning-curve arrays for both targets, all models, and sigma 0.0/0.3.

nodes.label: Full Bias-Variance Lab Script
nodes.rationale: The fuller implementation combines analytical numerical integration, Monte Carlo simulation, plot generation, and JSON persistence.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance Slide Generator
nodes.rationale: Builds a PowerPoint presentation containing setup, result tables, plots, and key findings.

nodes.label: Interactive Generalization and Learning-Curve Playground
nodes.rationale: A browser UI with Plotly visualizations, model controls, resampling, ensemble simulation, and learning-curve comparison.

nodes.label: Week 3 Bias-Variance README
nodes.rationale: Documents the assignment, decomposition theory, numerical methods, results, plot interpretations, and execution instructions.

nodes.label: Average-Fit Visualization
nodes.rationale: A 2 by 3 chart grid: rows are sin(pi*x) and x^2; columns are Constant, Linear, and Linear through origin. Green is the target, red dashed is g_bar(x), red shading is plus/minus one standard deviation, and faint gray curves show sampled hypotheses.

nodes.label: Combined Learning-Curve Visualization
nodes.rationale: A 2 by 3 chart grid of Expected Error versus logarithmic training size n. Dashed curves are Ein and solid curves are Eout, with separate sigma 0.0 and sigma 0.3 traces for each target/model pair.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance Decomposition
nodes.rationale: The documented decomposition treats expected out-of-sample error as integrated bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise variance.

nodes.label: Learning Curves
nodes.rationale: Learning curves compare Ein and Eout as n grows over [2,3,4,5,7,10,15,20,30,50,100] and under multiple noise levels.

nodes.label: Target Function sin(pi*x)
nodes.rationale: One of the two target functions; its odd symmetry makes the constant-model mean zero and exposes high variance in the unconstrained linear model at n=2.

nodes.label: Target Function x^2
nodes.rationale: The even symmetric target for which the constant model has the lowest reported Eout because its mean approximates the target well over Uniform[-1,1].

nodes.label: Constant Model
nodes.rationale: Fits h(x)=b using the mean response. Its low variance makes it especially effective for the symmetric x^2 target.

nodes.label: Linear Model
nodes.rationale: Fits h(x)=w0+w1*x. With two points it can interpolate noiseless training data, yielding near-zero Ein but potentially very high variance and Eout.

nodes.label: Linear Through Origin Model
nodes.rationale: Fits h(x)=w*x without an intercept, reducing flexibility and variance while imposing additional bias when the target is not well represented by an origin-constrained line.

nodes.label: Uniform[-1,1] Sampling
nodes.rationale: The training and test-domain expectation is based on x sampled uniformly from [-1,1], with density 1/2.

nodes.label: Normal-Equation Least Squares
nodes.rationale: Model fitting uses numpy.linalg.lstsq rather than gradient descent.

nodes.label: Analytical Numerical Integration
nodes.rationale: The analytical path approximates expectations with dense-grid trapezoidal integration and Monte Carlo integration over training datasets.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo Simulation
nodes.rationale: The simulation path fits many randomly sampled datasets and estimates g_bar, bias squared, variance, and Eout on test points.

nodes.label: Two-Point Training Setting
nodes.rationale: Bias-variance results use n=2 training samples; learning curves vary n beyond this base setting.

nodes.label: Learning-Curve Noise Levels
nodes.rationale: The supplied compact/results pipeline evaluates sigma 0.0 and 0.3; the README also describes a 0.1 level in the broader assignment setup.

nodes.label: Bias Squared Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures the squared distance between the average hypothesis and the true target, integrated over x.

nodes.label: Variance Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures the spread of hypotheses trained on different datasets around the average hypothesis.

nodes.label: Expected Out-of-Sample Error Eout
nodes.rationale: The reported error combines bias squared, variance, and sigma squared when noisy observations are used.

nodes.label: Average Hypothesis g_bar(x)
nodes.rationale: The mean prediction over datasets is visualized against the target and used to calculate bias squared.

nodes.label: Compact fit_predict Function
nodes.rationale: Dispatches among constant, full linear, and origin-constrained least-squares predictions.

nodes.label: Compact simulate Function
nodes.rationale: Generates 50,000 two-point datasets, aggregates predictions, and returns bias squared, variance, Eout, g_bar, and standard deviation arrays.

nodes.label: Compact learning_curve Function
nodes.rationale: Averages training and test MSE over 3,000 datasets for each n and sigma.

nodes.label: Compact Plotting Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Runs the experiment over target/model combinations and saves the combined average-fit and learning-curve images.

nodes.label: safe_fit_linear Function
nodes.rationale: Fits a line through two points and handles nearly coincident x values with a fallback.

nodes.label: gD Linear Hypothesis Function
nodes.rationale: Constructs the two-point full linear hypothesis used by analytical_model.

nodes.label: gD Linear-Origin Hypothesis Function
nodes.rationale: Constructs the origin-constrained two-point hypothesis and guards against a near-zero denominator.

nodes.label: analytical_constant Function
nodes.rationale: Uses E[f], E[f^2], and the n=2 closed-form variance relationship for the constant model.

nodes.label: analytical_model Function
nodes.rationale: Selects the analytical hypothesis family, samples x1/x2, computes g_bar and E_D[g_D^2], then integrates bias and variance.

nodes.label: simulate_bias_variance Function
nodes.rationale: The noisy Monte Carlo estimator of the decomposition, defaulting to n_samples=2 and 50,000 datasets.

nodes.label: Full learning_curve Function
nodes.rationale: Computes average Ein and Eout for each training size, including Gaussian response noise.

nodes.label: Full Lab Results Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Coordinates analytical and simulation results, plots, learning curves, and writing results.json.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance Updated Presentation
nodes.rationale: The slide sequence presents experimental setup, target-specific tables, visualizations, and conclusions.

nodes.label: Generalization Playground
nodes.rationale: Interactive browser section for Ein/Eout, average fit, bias squared, variance, and model comparison.

nodes.label: Learning Curve Playground
nodes.rationale: Interactive browser section for theory, practice, and simple-versus-complex learning-curve comparison.

nodes.label: Simple-versus-Complex Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: The UI highlights the lowest Eout and explicitly notes that it is often not the most complex model.

nodes.label: Browser fitModel Function
nodes.rationale: Dispatches browser-side fitting to constant, linear, or linear-origin implementations.

nodes.label: Browser renderGenCmp Function
nodes.rationale: Runs an ensemble for all three browser models, computes bias/variance/Eout, and renders comparison plots and a table.

nodes.label: Browser curveFor Function
nodes.rationale: Computes Ein, bias squared, variance, and Eout over the fixed learning-curve sizes for one browser model.

nodes.label: Browser renderLcCurve Function
nodes.rationale: Renders Ein and Eout curves, model comparison traces, and the bias-squared plus noise asymptote.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance Results Dataset
nodes.rationale: Contains analytical and simulation metrics for both targets and all three models.

nodes.label: Learning-Curve Results Dataset
nodes.rationale: Contains Ein/Eout arrays across n for sigma 0.0 and 0.3.
